properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 10 at 12:55PM PST until November 16 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet with dangerous rip
currents. These waves are expected to significantly increase
Friday into the weekend. Minor tidal overflows are possible
during morning high tides.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A significant westerly swell is expected
this weekend with impacts likely peaking Saturday. There is
potential for warning-level surf, significant beach erosion and
enhanced coastal flooding risk. Posing most risk to west-facing
beaches. Coastal hazards are likely to continue well into next
week.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Los Angeles County Beaches; Los Angeles County Inland Coast including Downtown Los Angeles
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 10 at 12:18PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne and
Manhattan Beach. Levels of particle pollution can vary by time and
location depending on emissions and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 11:59 PM Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 10 at 12:11PM PST until November 13 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco including bayshore locations along the
San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high
tide is expected to be: 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at
11:35 AM Wednesday 11/11, 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at
12:10 PM Thursday 11/12, 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at
12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.4 ft
of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later
along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 10 at 11:14AM PST until November 16 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected for elevations above 6000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to a foot, with up to 2 feet at the highest peaks.
Minor accumulations of around an 1 inch possible down to 5000 feet.
Winds could gust as high as 60 mph.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 6000 feet, including Highway 50,
Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108. Southern Cascades
above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Friday evening and Monday morning commutes. Strong
winds could cause downed tree branches and localized power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels 7000 to 8000 feet Friday, lowering
to 6500 feet Saturday, then down to around 5000 feet by Monday
morning. Heaviest snowfall expected Friday night into Saturday
morning. Light flurries to a dusting possible down to 5000 feet
with measurable accumulations remaining above 6000 feet. There
could be a break during the day Saturday, followed by additional
snow Saturday night into Monday.
properties.instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.
